content: #1 In the opening paragraph of the page for pseudocompact rings pseudocompact+ring it claims that a pseudocompact ring is a "regular pro-object in Artinian rings". I came here specifically to check my belief that the category of pseudocompact rings was precisely the procategory of the category of Artinian rings (and nlab is the first google hit for pseudocompact rings) but this word "regular" has thrown me. Is it just a decorative adjective or is it a mathematically contentful adjective being applied to "pro-object"? If so, can someone tell me what a regular pro-object is?
subject: "regular pro-object"?

content:
#2 To me it looks like “regular” is spurious here, but best to check with the author of this line: it is due to Zoran Škoda (in revision 1 from January 2011).

[edit: Maybe “regular” was meant as in “ordinary”, hence as in “it is just a pro-object”.]
subject: "regular pro-object"?

content: #3 The terminology appears to originate in the 1971 paper Equational completion, model induced triples and pro-objects by J.F. Kennison and Dion Gildenhuys. See the definition on page 327, which clarifies what “regular” means here.
subject: "regular pro-object"?

content: #4 In Gildenhuys and Kennison they mention: given d.c.c. for subalgebras, all pro- objects are regular. The condition is well known but perhaps under another name. I do not have the sources (prior to that 1971 paper) at hand.
subject: "regular pro-object"?

content: #5 I have found the term ‘essentially epimorphic’ used in J.-L. Verdier, Équivalence essentielle des systemes projectifs, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, 261, (1965), 4950–4953. This is more or less the same except epimorphism is replaced by onto in the case of `regular’. It seems to be related to the Mittag-Lefler condition.
subject: "regular pro-object"?

content: #6 Yes, I wonder whether in my application (where the Artin local rings have fixed residue field) the condition is automatic. The question I was actually wondering was whether if we fix a finite field k, then the category of pseudocompact local rings equipped with an isomorphism of their residue field with k was equal to the pro-category of the category of Artin local rings equipped with an isomorphism of their residue field with k (in these categories all morphisms are local and induce the identity on k, i.e. k is the terminal object). In practice I am not entirely sure whether I need this result but I am setting up the deformation theory used in Wiles' proof of FLT, in Lean, and a concrete category is far easier to work with in practice than a pro-category. Originally Wiles just used a category of complete Noetherian local rings with residue field k and so probably the question doesn't matter.
subject: "regular pro-object"?
